In [[number theory]], a '''cyclotomic character''' is a [[Character (mathematics)#Multiplicative character|character]] of a [[Galois group]] giving the Galois [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] on a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] of [[roots of unity]]. As a one-dimensional [[Group representation|representation]] over a [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] {{math|''R''}}, its [[representation space]] is generally denoted by {{math|''R''(1)}} (that is, it is a representation {{math|{{nowrap|χ : ''G'' → Aut<sub>R</sub>(''R''(1)) ≈ GL(1, ''R'')}}}}).

==<span id="padic"></span>''p''-adic cyclotomic character==
Fix {{math|''p''}} a [[prime number|prime]], and let <math>G_\mathbf{Q}</math> denote the [[absolute Galois group]] of the [[rational number]]s. 
The roots of unity <math display="block">\mu_{p^n} = \left\{ \zeta \in \bar\mathbf{Q}^\times \mid \zeta^{p^n} = 1 \right\}</math> form a [[cyclic group]] of order <math>p^n</math>, generated by any choice of a [[Primitive root of unity|primitive]] {{math|''p''<sup>''n''</sup>}}th root of unity {{math|''ζ''<sub>''p''<sup>''n''</sup></sub>}}. 

Since all of the primitive roots in <math>\mu_{p^n}</math> are [[Galois conjugate]], the Galois group <math>G_\mathbf{Q}</math> acts on <math>\mu_{p^n}</math> by automorphisms. After fixing a primitive root of unity <math>\zeta_{p^n}</math> generating <math>\mu_{p^n}</math>, any element <math>\zeta\in\mu_{p^n}</math> can be written as a power of <math>\zeta_{p^n}</math>, where the exponent is a unique element in <math>\mathbf{Z}/p^n\mathbf{Z}</math>, which is a unit if <math>\zeta</math> is also primitive. One can thus write, for <math>\sigma\in G_\mathbf{Q}</math>,

<math display="block">\sigma.\zeta := \sigma(\zeta) = \zeta^{a(\sigma, n)}</math>

with <math>a(\sigma,n) \in (\mathbf{Z}/p^n \mathbf{Z})^\times</math> independent of <math>\zeta</math>, but depending on both <math>\sigma</math> and <math>p</math>. This defines a [[group homomorphism]] called the '''mod {{math|''p''<sup>''n''</sup>}} cyclotomic character''':

<math display="block">\begin{align}{\chi_{p^n}}:G_{\mathbf{Q}} &\to (\mathbf{Z}/p^n\mathbf{Z})^{\times} \\ \sigma &\mapsto a(\sigma, n), \end{align}</math>
which is viewed as a [[Character_(mathematics)|character]] since the action corresponds to a homomorphism <math>G_{\mathbf Q} \to \mathrm{Aut}(\mu_{p^n}) \cong (\mathbf{Z}/p^n\mathbf{Z})^\times \cong \mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbf{Z}/p^n\mathbf{Z})</math>.

Fixing <math>p</math> and <math>\sigma</math> and varying <math>n</math>, the <math>a(\sigma, n)</math> form a compatible system in the sense that they give an element of the [[inverse limit]] <math display="block">\varprojlim_n 
 (\mathbf{Z}/p^n\mathbf{Z})^\times \cong \mathbf{Z}_p^\times,</math>the units in the ring of [[P-adic_number|p-adic integers]]. Thus the <math>{\chi_{p^n}}</math> assemble to a [[group homomorphism]] called '''{{math|''p''}}-adic cyclotomic character''':

<math display="block">\begin{align} \chi_p:G_{\mathbf Q} &\to \mathbf{Z}_p^\times \cong \mathrm{GL_1}(\mathbf{Z}_p) \\ \sigma &\mapsto (a(\sigma, n))_n \end{align}</math>
encoding the action of <math>G_{\mathbf Q}</math> on all {{math|''p''}}-power roots of unity <math>\mu_{p^n}</math> simultaneously. In fact equipping <math>G_{\mathbf Q}</math> with the [[Krull topology]] and <math>\mathbf{Z}_p</math> with the [[p-adic|{{math|''p''}}-adic]] topology makes this a continuous representation of a [[topological group]].

==As a compatible system of {{math|ℓ}}-adic representations==
By varying {{math|ℓ}} over all prime numbers, a [[compatible system of ℓ-adic representations]] is obtained from the {{math|ℓ}}-adic cyclotomic characters (when considering compatible systems of representations, the standard terminology is to use the symbol {{math|ℓ}} to denote a prime instead of {{math|''p''}}). That is to say, {{math|1=χ = { χ<sub>ℓ</sub> }<sub>ℓ</sub>}} is a "family" of {{math|ℓ}}-adic representations

:<math>\chi_\ell:G_\mathbf{Q}\rightarrow\operatorname{GL}_1(\mathbf{Z}_\ell)</math>

satisfying certain compatibilities between different primes. In fact, the {{math|χ<sub>ℓ</sub>}} form a [[strictly compatible system of ℓ-adic representations]].

==Geometric realizations== <!-- Note: Tate motive redirects here -->
The {{math|''p''}}-adic cyclotomic character is the {{math|''p''}}-adic [[Tate module]] of the [[Algebraic torus|multiplicative group scheme]] {{math|'''G'''<sub>''m'','''Q'''</sub>}} over {{math|'''Q'''}}. As such, its representation space can be viewed as the [[inverse limit]] of the groups of {{math|''p''<sup>''n''</sup>}}th roots of unity in {{math|{{Overline|'''Q'''}}}}.

In terms of [[étale cohomology|cohomology]], the {{math|''p''}}-adic cyclotomic character is the [[Duality (mathematics)|dual]] of the first {{math|''p''}}-adic [[étale cohomology]] group of {{math|'''G'''<sub>''m''</sub>}}. It can also be found in the étale cohomology of a [[projective variety]], namely the [[projective line]]: it is the dual of {{math|''H''<sup>2</sup><sub>ét</sub>('''P'''<sup>1</sup> )}}.

In terms of [[Motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]], the {{math|''p''}}-adic cyclotomic character is the {{math|''p''}}-adic realization of the '''Tate motive''' {{math|'''Z'''(1)}}. As a [[Grothendieck motive]], the Tate motive is the dual of {{math|''H''<sup>2</sup>( '''P'''<sup>1</sup> )}}.<ref>Section 3 of {{Citation

==Properties==
The {{math|''p''}}-adic cyclotomic character satisfies several nice properties.

*It is [[unramified]] at all primes {{math|ℓ ≠ ''p''}} (i.e. the [[inertia subgroup]] at {{math|ℓ}} acts trivially).
*If {{math|Frob<sub>ℓ</sub>}} is a [[Frobenius element]] for {{math|ℓ ≠ ''p''}}, then {{math|1=χ<sub>p</sub>(Frob<sub>ℓ</sub>) =&nbsp;ℓ}}.
*It is [[Crystalline_representation|crystalline]] at {{math|''p''}}.
